text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- Swiss youth hostels, hit by a broad slump in tourism in Switzerland, are making a comeback by adapting more relaxed and varied policies. Innovations include staying open later at night, offering sports and providing family holidays. - Gas station operators in Ticino, Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton, are afraid of proposals in the neighbouring Italian region of Lombardy to cut retail fuel prices. Gas in Switzerland has traditionaly been cheaper than in Italy, bringing Ticino sellers a steady cross-border trade that could dwindle if Lombardy lowers prices.

- Pension and early retirement costs mean the Swiss federal government may have to pay more than planned for the coming reform of the state railroad monopoly SBB. The railroad is supposed to be reorganised to make it more competitive and profitable under legislation expected to take effect in 1999 or later. But SBB and the state have to find a way to cover a gap of five billion Swiss francs in the railroad's pension needs. - Credit Suisse Group, which in April became the first Swiss bank to offer Internet retail banking, had attracted 5,000 customers as of June. The product "Direct net" allows retail customers to make payments and buy and sell securities over the Internet.
- Swiss labour leader Vasco Pedrina called for controls on what he views as rampant black market labour in the country. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
